correctness.rationale: The host H_K(v)=pi_1^K v_1 pi_2^K...v_(m-1)pi_m^K (pi_i permutes alphabet without v_i) avoids v under greedy matching and contains each length<=K v-avoiding word by decomposing it at greedy matches into alphabet-restricted blocks. The insertion sphere of length-(k-1) pattern has (q-1)k+1 distinct k-word elements, proved by moving identical letters through runs and Parikh-vector uniqueness; each absent shorter subsequence forces those longer absences and H_k(v) attains the bound. For unary v=a^m and K>=m, an avoiding universal host contains exactly m-1 a letters; every gap must contain each length t=K-m+1 non-a constant word, giving the sharp lower m(q-1)t+m-1, attained by permutation^t blocks. Independent literal subsequence checks covered 2626 cases and brute-force unary shortest lengths, while packaged verify.py enumerates additional finite samples. K=0/m=1 boundaries were examined. Infinite assertions rest on constructions and lower bounds.

originality.rationale: Classical Higman–Haines ideals establish qualitative subsequence-avoidance structure, while Fleischmann et al. (2022) study m-nearly-k-universal words and sharp missing-one-word cases. The assessed contribution is an explicit universal bounded host for every principal avoidance class plus the exact all-alphabet insertion-sphere defect jump and unary optimal length. The Resultary full-support insertion-radius finding measures a different operation (letters inserted to reach full universality). Prior structural theory may imply host existence but the sharp quantitative unary cost and entire spectrum were not observed in inspected statements.
